newsitem.title: USA: Group asks SEC to probe Duke, PanEnergy merger.
newsitem.headline: Group asks SEC to probe Duke, PanEnergy merger.

text.p: Consumer advocates Citizen Action Tuesday urged the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to review the proposed $7.7 billion merger of Duke Power Co with PanEnergy Corp.
The group said the merger to form Duke Energy could run afoul of Duke Power's existing exemption from the Public Utility Holding Company Act.

"If the proposed merger becomes final, the post-merger corporate structure appears to be inconsistent with and contrary to Duke Power's present exemption from PUHCA," Citizen Action's energy policy director Edwin Rothschild said in a letter to the SEC.
If Duke Energy were to lose the exemption, "then the SEC ... must require Duke Energy to divest itself of PanEnergy and any non-utility businesses," he said.
PUHCA was designed to protect utility investors from subsidizing utility holding company unprofitable ventures in unrelated businesses.
"It is clear that the merged company, Duke Energy, cannot be described as predominantly a public utility holding company ..., which will place the exemption at risk," Rothschild said.
A spokesman for Duke Power said the issue had been raised before, but "we don't think we're under any danger of losing our exemption under the holding company act."
